Quick rundown of my job.

I work for a large call center company who was recently contracted by a large bank to handle their welfare program.

The way Welfare actually works is as follows: The State contacts a large bank and asks the bank "Hey, can you put together a shit ton of prepaid debit card accounts? We can't manage this on our own." The Bank, not wanting to turn away money tells the state "Sure!" and creates their special program, with prepaid debit cards to be sent to anybody in The State who is on welfare, in this case, child support and unemployment.

MY job is to help the recipients of welfare manage their accounts. You can guess who the majority of my clientele are.

This job SUCKS. I speak to about 150 people per 8 hour shift. There is no downtime between calls. Of the 150 people I speak to, maybe 5-6 of them can form a sentence without using made up words or grammar mistakes. The rest of them can't speak properly to save their fucking lives. Just as an example, the most common thing I hear. "I was callin to aks where mah muhney at?" Now imagine the person on the other end of the line has their phone IN their mouth, rather than near. This is my day.

I speak to the poor, and the downtrodden for a living. And you know what they spend "their" welfare money on? Booze. Superficial shit. Fast Food. "Gettin they nails did." It is not unusual for me to speak with a mother of three or four kids wondering where her money's gone, only to find out that she spent it all on alcohol.

Now, pair this level of bullshit with an entitled attitude. I tell that mom I mentioned earlier what's happened to her money, and she freaks the fuck out. "You's just callin me a liar cuz I never spunt mah money on dat sheeit. Yous a rasis. Get me yo managa." Manager gets on line, and tells the cardholder that they did indeed spend all of the money on shit that the didn't need, and no, we cannot give them more to pay their bills. This is not an unusual call.

Most commonly, I replace lost cards. The morons who receive these cards never think to update their addresses with the state, so we have to update them at the same time as ordering a new card. This means that the cardholder MUST submit a fax to our office, providing proof of who they are, and forms of address verification such as bills. Now, a fax is cheap. If you don't have a fax machine, but you have a smart-phone, you actually have access to a fax machine. This means that the cardholder might need to take some time out of their day if they want access to their funds. This is apocalyptic to them. "I is who I say I is, why I gotta submit a fax? Ain't nobody got a fax no more." is a common statement. So I explain. "Sir/Ma'am, the reason we need the fax is to prevent anybody who is pretending to be you from just changing your address and stealing your funds." and the usual response? "You mean like you is right now?"

They do not understand basic security. It is EASY to steal these cards due to the fucking stupidity of the cardholder. You steal their purse or wallet? Guess what, you have everything you need to steal their card and account. Fraud happens on these cards so frequently because security has to be so poor, lest the idiot holding the card lock themselves out.

Another common theme of this program is abuse. For some reason, despite my title being Cardholder Services Representative, and this being my paid job, the cardholder gets it in their tiny fucking skull that I don't want to help them, and that I am actively preventing them from getting what they want. So, rather than actually listening to me, or anybody else on my floor, they get angry. They scream obscenities and insults at us, and insist that they speak to managers, who tell them exactly what we already told them.

We don't have a hangup script. We must eat the shit with a smile on our faces, lest our attitude on the phone drops, and we lose points on our quality scores.

The scores are strict, as expected of a call center. Make one grammar mistake, or forget one piece of information, you will lose points. Your attitude droops from "chipper motherfucker happy to help regardless of the issue" even slightly, you lose points. You forget to say thank you after they shit in your mouth? Lose points. Say the intro wrong? Points gone. It is easy to fail at this job, and nigh impossible to get a full 100 on the QA score. You will be marked off for something, because you will get something wrong. It's just a fact. You CANNOT meet the client's expectations, because the client has impossible standards, particularly regarding notes. There is no downtime between calls. If you do not accurately notate your call, meaning write literally everything that happened during your call down in a note in the system, you will lose points. Forget a period in those notes? Points gone. Grammatically incorrect? Points gone. The notes have such stringent standards because they can, and DO get subpoenaed by the feds, regularly.

Its not just me, but everyone who have bought this tablet and made the OTA upgrade is [suffering from the same fate](http://www.asus.com/zentalk/in/forum.php?mod=viewthread&tid=59750). The most troublesome aspect of this is that the OEM stopped giving new updates just after this last buggy OTA update.

Of course, like most of you people, I may have to forget about it and keep saying, "OEMs can do whatever they want", but that isn't going to stop me from trying. Call me a socialist or SJW, but the least I want to do is make sure that the OEMs think twice before giving out a half-baked OTA update that breaks an existing working device. And I believe that it can happen if enough people will sign this petition:

https://www.change.org/p/asustek-please-fix-the-battery-drain-issue-in-your-latest-ota-update-v6-3-9-for-fonepad-me175cg?recruiter=337404987&utm_source=share_petition&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=share_email_responsive

On the long end that could be 20 years for someone lucky. We'd be lucky to expect 5 years of them cairing about the product. The answer is to not be dependent on an OEM to control what patches are applied to a device.

For now let's get that petition signed. But, hey, it is on you for buying a product that had a bloatware version of android as the OS. I know that's common, but dumb. Bloatware as OS is the fault of the consumer for facilitating.
